Approaching the 300 Metres made contact with JOLLY COMPANION due to both runners shifting ground. Apprentice H Y Yuen stated that after leading the event her mount failed to run on in the Home Straight and was disappointing. Trainer Y S Tsui advised that the horse had pleased him leading into the race and he was of the opinion that Apprentice Yuen had to make too much use of the horse in the early stages to lead and this was the principal reason for the horse’s disappointing performance. A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings. The performance of GIMME FIVE was considered disappointing. Before being allowed to race again, GIMME FIVE will be required to perform to the satisfaction of the Stewards in a barrier trial and be subjected to an official veterinary examination.

Approaching the 300 Metres made contact with GIMME FIVE due to both runners shifting ground. Z Purton stated that after obtaining a position outside the lead his mount failed to respond to his riding in the Home Straight but could offer no excuse for the horse’s disappointing performance. Trainer K L Man advised that the horse had pleased him leading into the race and he had instructed Jockey Purton to go forward from its wide barrier. He added the only explanation he could offer for the horse’s disappointing performance was that too much use had to be made of the horse in the early stages to go forward. A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings. The performance of JOLLY COMPANION was considered disappointing. Before being allowed to race again, JOLLY COMPANION will be required to perform to the satisfaction of the Stewards in a barrier trial and be subjected to an official veterinary examination.

Before being allowed to race again, MAGIC SUPER will be required to perform to the satisfaction of the Stewards in a barrier trial and be subjected to an official veterinary examination which must include additional diagnostic assessments. A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.

Jumped awkwardly and lost ground. Apprentice H Y Yuen stated that the horse did not appreciate the kickback in the early stages on the All Weather surface.

When questioned regarding his riding of CALA DEI MORI and the reason he rode his mount forward to race outside BUSTLING CITY, E C W Wong confirmed that his instructions were to go forward and take up a position behind the expected leaders BUSTLING CITY and LUCY IN THE SKY. He said as his mount does have a tendency to jump fairly he ensured that CALA DEI MORI jumped well and then rode his mount along in the early stages to comply with his instructions. He said after riding his mount along and when caught wide to the outside of LUCY IN THE SKY, CALA DEI MORI, which was racing in blinkers for the first time, then commenced to race keenly and as a result he improved forward of LUCY IN THE SKY to race outside BUSTLING CITY. He added in the early stages CALA DEI MORI would not settle and as a result the pace of the event was run faster than he would have preferred, however, his mount would not respond to his efforts to set a more sustainable pace. He said from the 800 Metres CALA DEI MORI settled better and he was able to restrain the horse to obtain a position further back from BUSTLING CITY. Trainer C S Shum confirmed the instructions were to obtain a position with cover behind the expected leaders and agreed that CALA DEI MORI raced keenly with blinkers being applied for the first time. After considering his explanation the Stewards advised Jockey Wong that he had made an error of judgement in the early stages by riding his mount along which resulted in CALA DEI MORI racing too keenly, particularly as he was aware that the horse had raced keenly in its two barrier trials on 19 September 2026 and 2 October 2026 when it wore blinkers on those occasions. Jockey Wong was further advised that in similar circumstances he would be expected to show better judgement than what he did on this occasion so as to leave no room for query. A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.

The performance of DRAGON JOY, which finished tailed out, was considered unacceptable. Before being allowed to race again, DRAGON JOY will be required to perform to the satisfaction of the Stewards in a barrier trial and be subjected to an official veterinary examination. A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.

When questioned regarding his riding of CALA DEI MORI and the reason he rode his mount forward to race outside BUSTLING CITY, E C W Wong confirmed that his instructions were to go forward and take up a position behind the expected leaders BUSTLING CITY and LUCY IN THE SKY. He said as his mount does have a tendency to jump fairly he ensured that CALA DEI MORI jumped well and then rode his mount along in the early stages to comply with his instructions. He said after riding his mount along and when caught wide to the outside of LUCY IN THE SKY, CALA DEI MORI, which was racing in blinkers for the first time, then commenced to race keenly and as a result he improved forward of LUCY IN THE SKY to race outside BUSTLING CITY. He added in the early stages CALA DEI MORI would not settle and as a result the pace of the event was run faster than he would have preferred, however, his mount would not respond to his efforts to set a more sustainable pace. He said from the 800 Metres CALA DEI MORI settled better and he was able to restrain the horse to obtain a position further back from BUSTLING CITY. Trainer C S Shum confirmed the instructions were to obtain a position with cover behind the expected leaders and agreed that CALA DEI MORI raced keenly with blinkers being applied for the first time. After considering his explanation the Stewards advised Jockey Wong that he had made an error of judgement in the early stages by riding his mount along which resulted in CALA DEI MORI racing too keenly, particularly as he was aware that the horse had raced keenly in its two barrier trials on 19 September 2026 and 2 October 2026 when it wore blinkers on those occasions. Jockey Wong was further advised that in similar circumstances he would be expected to show better judgement than what he did on this occasion so as to leave no room for query. A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
